scope: engagement appointment controller, schema, entity, service and repository
engagement newsletter controller, routes, schema and the new signed unsubscribe token
reviewed_without_change: Reminder creation already uses the signed-in user; marking reminders sent and variant reminder listings are admin-only.
Scheduling and sending notifications are admin-only.
Appointment booking refuses past start times, end-before-start and overlapping appointments for the same customer.

findings.problem: Any signed-in user could read any reminder (contact preferences) by id, list any user's reminders, and unsubscribe or delete other customers' reminders.
findings.change: Customers see and change only their own reminders; staff may read any and customer care may change any; others get 404 (403 for user listings).
findings.verification: E2E: baseline another customer read the reminder (200); fixed 404/403 for others, owner and customer care keep access.

findings.problem: Appointments were booked under the userId in the body, and any signed-in user could read, reschedule or cancel any appointment and list any user's appointments.
findings.change: Customers book for themselves (store staff may book for a named customer); only the owner, staff (read) and store staff (change) can access an appointment.
findings.verification: E2E: baseline the appointment was stored under the other customer; fixed stored under the caller, other customers get 404/403, store staff booking for a customer works.

findings.problem: In-store appointments could never be booked: the domain value 'in-store' was passed to Prisma, whose enum key is in_store, so every in-store booking failed with a database error (and stored rows could not be read back).
findings.change: Appointment types are mapped to and from the database enum in the repository.
findings.verification: E2E: staff booking an in-store appointment returns 201 (previously 400 'Invalid database operation').

findings.problem: Rescheduling explicitly allowed moving an appointment into the past, although booking refuses past times.
findings.change: Rescheduling applies the same rule as booking.
findings.verification: Unit Appointment spec: baseline the past reschedule was accepted; fixed refused and the time unchanged.

findings.problem: Any signed-in user could read system notifications (payloads, recipients, errors) by id or type, while only admins can schedule or send them.

findings.file: newsletter controller, routes and schema; newsletter-unsubscribe-token.ts
findings.problem: Anyone could check whether an address was subscribed (and get its subscription id) and unsubscribe any address or subscription id without proof; the unsubscribe page inserted values into HTML without escaping.
findings.change: Unsubscribing requires the signed token from the unsubscribe link, a signed-in account with that email, or customer care; lookups are for the signed-in owner or customer care; subscription ids are staff-only; HTML output is escaped. createNewsletterUnsubscribeToken is provided for building links (secret NEWSLETTER_UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET, falling back to JWT_SECRET). API client regenerated.
findings.verification: E2E: baseline anonymous lookup and unsubscribe 200; fixed 403, forged link 400, signed link 200 and the subscription is unsubscribed, signed-in owner can still manage their own.

tests.new: E2E engagement-privacy (5), unit Appointment past-reschedule case (1); existing newsletter E2E now looks up the subscription as admin
tests.baseline: 5 of 6 new cases failed against the previous engagement code (stash baseline); the owner self-management case passed by design.
tests.database_suites: All E2E and integration suites: 163 tests in 47 files pass
tests.final: 1527 unit tests in 119 files; root/tooling tsc; 7/7 workspace type-checks (forced); engagement ESLint (no errors); API client regenerated and drift check passes

follow_ups: No code sends newsletters yet; when it does, links must use createNewsletterUnsubscribeToken. Subscribing has no double opt-in, so anyone can subscribe any address (owner decision; needs an email sender).
Stock-added handling simulates restock notifications instead of sending them (existing P01 follow-up); reminder delivery is not implemented.
Appointments have no store capacity or opening-hours rules.
